verses.text: Then Job answered:
"I know that's true. But how can anyone be in the right before God?
If someone wanted to argue a case with him, they couldn't answer him once in a thousand times.
God is wise and mighty. Who has ever set themselves against him and come out well?
He moves mountains before they know what's happening, overturning them in his anger.
He shakes the earth out of its place, and its pillars tremble.
He orders the sun to stay down and seals up the stars.
He alone stretches out the heavens and walks on the waves of the sea.
He made the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the hidden regions of the southern sky.
He does great things nobody can fathom, more wonders than anyone can count.
He passes by me, and I don't see him. He moves on, and I don't even notice.
When he takes something away, who can stop him? Who can ask him, 'What are you doing?'
God won't hold back his anger. Even Rahab's helpers bow beneath him.
How much less could I answer him or find the words to argue my case?
Even if I were in the right, I couldn't answer him. I'd have to plead for mercy from my judge.
Even if I called and he answered, I wouldn't believe he was listening to me.
He crushes me with a storm and gives me wound after wound for no reason.
He won't let me catch my breath. He fills me with bitterness.
If this is a contest of strength, he's the mighty one. If it's a matter for the court, he asks, 'Who will summon me?'
Even if I'm in the right, my own mouth will condemn me. Even if I'm blameless, I'll be declared guilty.
I am blameless. I've stopped caring what happens to me. I despise my life.
It all comes to the same thing. That's why I say he destroys both the blameless and the wicked.
When disaster kills without warning, he mocks the distress of the innocent.
The earth is handed over to the wicked, and he covers the eyes of its judges. If it isn't him, then who is it?
My days run faster than a runner. They flee without seeing anything good.
They slip away like swift boats, like an eagle swooping down on its prey.
If I say, 'I'll forget my complaint, take off this sad face, and cheer up,'
I'm still afraid of all my suffering. I know you won't declare me innocent.
I'm going to be condemned, so why wear myself out for nothing?
Even if I wash myself with snow and scrub my hands with lye,
you'll plunge me into a ditch, and even my own clothes will loathe me.
God isn't human like me. I can't answer him as if we could stand together in court.
There's no one to decide between us, no one who could lay a hand on both of us.
If only he would take his rod away from me and stop terrifying me,
then I could speak without being afraid of him. As things stand, I can't."
